newsitem.title: USA: Avocet Mining to restart Peru tungsten mine.
newsitem.headline: Avocet Mining to restart Peru tungsten mine.

text.p: Avocet Mining's tungsten division is to restart its Malaga mine in Peru within a month, Robert Bunting, president of Avocet Tungsten, Inc said.
Output was expected initially to be at 1,000 to 2,000 metric tonne units of W03 per month, or about 20 tonnes of gross concentrates product.
The concentrates will be converted into ammonium paratungstate (APT) at the company's Bishop mill in Californina.
"It's a small mine in the world picture of tungsten," Bunting said. "The real issues are that Chinese prices are rising."
"I am cautiously optimistic that tungsten demand will be good worldwide this year. If anything it's going to get better in Europe and Japan," Bunting said.
Global production was still below consumption and firmer prices will pull more metal from Russian stocks in particular.
"I expect to see more stuff coming out of stockpiles...but I think it will be relatively modest compared to what it was before," Bunting said.
